findings.found: Two questions framed their choices inconsistently — one carried a sentence on two options and not the other two, which gave the answer away; the other read as a sentence about shortening rather than as a word.
findings.action: Both reframed before the content was committed.
findings.foundBy: reading the generated choices back

automatedChecks.rule: Four distinct choices, exactly one of them the key, and the key is among them
No explanation names an answer by its position or letter, and no pack puts its keys at one position, four in a row, or in a repeating cycle
Twenty-four objects in the roles a lesson expects, every item passes validateContent, and a worked example can never be answered

No pack or item cites a Grade 5/6 outcome; every Alberta placement quotes statements that resolve word for word against curriculum.k6.json, cites pages the extraction gives that organizing idea, and states the grade range the ladder derives
Every question is answered by looking: no spoken text, no audio asset, no audio status on any item or option
The explanations of each pack read at Grade 7 or below by the readability formula
Nothing is released, and no item carries a status a parent did not grant

findings.found: The question asking for the word that starts with a cluster offered whip as a wrong answer, calling wh one sound. Some speakers say the wh in whip as two sounds, and for them whip starts with a cluster too, so the question had two defensible answers.
findings.action: whip replaced with chin, which starts with the digraph ch for every speaker.
findings.foundBy: reading every option against the rule the pack states

findings.found: The question asked which two letters make ONE sound in phone. The final e is silent, so n and e together also give one sound, and a careful child could defend that option.
findings.action: The question now asks which two letters make the f sound, which only p and h do.
findings.foundBy: reading every option against the rule the pack states

findings.found: A wrong option was gene, and its common error said that dropping the r from green gives gene. Gene starts with a j sound, not a g sound, so the stated error was false.
findings.action: gene replaced with grain, and the common error now names the vowel mistake that gives grin or grain.
findings.foundBy: reading every common error back as a claim to be checked

findings.scope: f2.sp.inflections.18, f2.pack.sp.inflections rule and help steps
findings.found: The pack teaches doubling the last consonant after one short vowel, which applied to fox gives foxxes, one of the wrong options. Neither the rule nor the explanation said that x is never doubled, so a child following the rule exactly would be marked wrong.
findings.action: The rule, the help step and the explanation now say x is never doubled, and a common error names the mistake.
findings.foundBy: applying the stated rule to every keyed word

findings.found: The question asked which chunk of disagreement is the base word, but the pack defines a chunk as having one vowel sound, and agree has two, so the question contradicted the pack’s own definition.
findings.action: Reworded to ask for the base word, like every other base-word question in the pack.
findings.foundBy: reading every prompt against the pack’s own terms

findings.found: The first draft of these F2 records named checks held by test files that never load the F2 packs (the punctuation, sentence and C1 pack tests, and a snapshot of the C0 ids only), and listed four findings about earlier drafts that were never committed, so nothing in the repository could show them.
findings.action: The F2 records now name only tests that load the F2 packs, and list only defects found in the committed draft, each visible in the git history.
findings.foundBy: checking which test files import packs.foundation2.draft.js
